{"design":{"comparison_approach":"In-process Rust A/B microbench replaying ONE deterministic sequence of frame-byte buffers through two transports, so the only variable is marshalling. Lane A (C lane): the real wiring from app_lifecycle_ffi.rs — invoke an `extern \"C\" fn(*mut c_void, *const u8, usize)` through the same `Arc<dyn Fn(&[u8])>` closure shape (UpdateListener), zero-copy ptr/len, PLUS one representative \"shell consume\" memcpy out of the transient slice (mandatory for fairness: the real contract says the slice is valid only for the callback duration, so every real host copies once). Lane B (UniFFI lane): link the REAL `uniffi` runtime crate and exercise its actual lowering path for `Vec<u8>` — `RustBuffer::from_vec` (real alloc + memcpy) + `FfiConverter::<Vec<u8>>::lower` + an indirect vtable call into a Rust-implemented foreign-trait callback stub that performs the lower-bound foreign consume (memcpy RustBuffer contents into an owned Vec, then free), mirroring what Swift/Kotlin do when building a Data/ByteArray. Same buffers, same order, same allocator for both lanes. Subtract a measured empty-harness baseline (timer + index, no transport) from each. Verdict computed against a pre-registered rule.","whats_synthetic":"REAL (linked, executed, measured): the C-lane indirect call + ptr/len + shell copy; the UniFFI Rust-side cost — RustBuffer allocation, the FfiConverter lowering memcpy, and the indirect vtable callback dispatch — because we link the genuine `uniffi` crate rather than hand-simulating it. SYNTHETIC, explicitly labeled in the report as a LOWER BOUND: (1) the managed-runtime copy from RustBuffer into a real Swift `Data` / Kotlin `ByteArray` plus ARC/GC bookkeeping — modeled as a single plain memcpy+free, which is the floor of the true cost; (2) the JNI boundary surcharge (GetByteArrayElements/SetByteArrayRegion, local-ref table) — NOT executed; applied only as a pre-registered conservative multiplier band from published JNI numbers; (3) real cross-language thread/dispatch-queue handoff and on-device backpressure drop/reorder — not modeled (in-process drop/reorder is 0 by construction and reported as such, not as a real-transport claim). This is honest because the decision only needs to know whether marshalling is a small O(frame-bytes) constant or something pathological; the synthetic pieces can only make UniFFI look CHEAPER than reality, and the decision rule forbids a collapse verdict on synthetic evidence unless the surcharged estimate is comfortably under budget (otherwise it escalates to a real foreign-side measurement).","workload_model":"ADR-0055 diff-shaped, omit-unchanged regime. Three size buckets, deterministic fixed buffers (random transport is fine since transport carries opaque bytes; sizes chosen from the real encoder envelope + visible-window=80): SMALL incremental diff 256 B–2 KB (1–3 changed typed-projection sidecar entries), MEDIUM batch/scroll diff 2–8 KB, LARGE full snapshot 16–64 KB (account switch / epoch bump of the <=80-item visible window). Weighted mix 80% small / 15% medium / 5% large (omit-unchanged makes small dominant). Cadence grounded in code: steady 4 Hz (DEFAULT_EMIT_HZ), burst to 12 Hz (clamp ceiling); a reconnect catch-up burst train of back-to-back frames then steady. Volume: 100k deliveries per bucket per lane (after 10k warmup discarded) for stable p99; identical PRNG-seeded size/order sequence shared byte-for-byte across both lanes.","decision_rule":"PRE-REGISTERED before any measurement, expressed as % of a 60fps render-frame budget (16.67 ms) because the callback sits on the UI-thread handoff. Metric = weighted p99 of (UniFFI per-frame cost minus C-lane per-frame cost), with the synthetic foreign-copy component multiplied by a pre-registered conservative JNI/managed surcharge factor of 3x before comparison. Bands: COLLAPSE to one UniFFI surface (delete the internal byte lane) iff surcharged weighted-p99 delta < 5% of 16.67 ms (< 833 us/frame) AND absolute UniFFI p99 for the SMALL bucket < 250 us; KEEP an internal-only byte lane (justified, hidden behind UniFFI, with owner + delete/retest trigger) iff surcharged weighted-p99 delta >= 15% (>= 2.50 ms/frame); ESCALATE to a real Swift/Kotlin on-device A/B before deciding for anything in the 5–15% band. No collapse verdict is permitted from synthetic evidence inside or above the escalate band.","metrics":["p50 / p95 / p99 per-frame transport cost per size bucket and weighted (batch-of-K derived for sub-microsecond small bucket; empty-harness baseline subtracted)","weighted-p99 UniFFI-minus-C delta, raw and after 3x foreign-surcharge, vs the pre-registered % -of-60fps-budget threshold","allocations/frame and allocated-bytes/frame per lane (separate allocation-mode pass under CountingAllocator)","bytes/frame carried (buckets + weighted)","dropped/reordered frames = 0 by in-process construction, reported with explicit 'not a real-transport claim' caveat","thread-handoff note: in-process single listener thread; cross-language hop deferred/labeled","pre-registered verdict: COLLAPSE / KEEP-INTERNAL / ESCALATE with the governing number"],"confounders":"Warmup: discard first 10k iterations/lane to reach steady allocator+cache state (mirrors reactivity-bench steady-state split). Release-only: build/run --release, debug-assertions off; record rustc version, opt-level, lto, codegen-units in the report. Allocator: identical System-backed CountingAllocator for both lanes so deltas are fair — but run TWO passes: a timing pass with NO instrumentation (counting-allocator atomics would dwarf sub-us signal) and a separate allocation pass under CountingAllocator; never mix. Measurement overhead: Instant::now() (~20–40 ns) is large vs sub-us calls, so small-bucket percentiles are batch-of-K (K=1000) timed then divided, and an empty-harness baseline (timer+index, no transport) is subtracted from every lane. Thread: single-threaded, no tokio; pin to one core on Linux CI (best-effort/declared-unpinned on macOS, compensated by high iteration count + percentiles). Fairness: C lane MUST include the mandatory one shell-copy-out so zero-work C isn't compared against copy-heavy UniFFI.","location_tooling":"Hand-rolled bench binary, NOT criterion — matches the repo's established pattern (crates/nmp-testing/bin/reactivity-bench, firehose-bench: CountingAllocator + JSON report + gate-constant config + p50/p99), avoids criterion's heavy deps and per-iter harness overhead at sub-us scale, and emits a deterministic JSON report that feeds #2125 directly. New crate path: crates/nmp-testing/bin/ffi-transport-bench/, split like reactivity-bench (main.rs / config.rs / report.rs / allocator.rs) to stay under the 500-LOC gate. It `use`s nmp_native_runtime::UpdateListener and the real extern-\"C\" callback shape from nmp-ffi, links the real `uniffi` crate for lowering, and sources representative frame bytes via nmp_core::update_envelope encoders / fixed buffers. Scoped commands only: `cargo run -p nmp-testing --bin ffi-transport-bench --release -- --standard` plus the always-on `cargo test -p nmp-testing --test doctrine_lint_smoke`; never cargo test --workspace. Feeding #2125: the bench writes a JSON report under docs/perf/ with all percentiles, allocs/frame, bytes/frame, the surcharged delta, and the COLLAPSE/KEEP/ESCALATE verdict; a short interpretation comment is posted to #2125 quoting the weighted-p99 surcharged delta as a % of the 16.67 ms budget and the resulting verdict, with the synthetic-components caveat block.","v1_scope":"Smallest honest v1: single-process release Rust bench, two lanes over one deterministic shared frame-byte sequence — Lane A the real extern-\"C\" ptr/len indirection + mandatory shell copy; Lane B the REAL uniffi RustBuffer lowering + real vtable dispatch + a lower-bound Rust foreign-consume stub. Three size buckets + weighted mix, 4/12 Hz cadence model, p50/p95/p99 + allocs/frame + bytes/frame, empty-harn

Assistant: **The benchmark verdict is in: COLLAPSE — pure UniFFI, no internal byte lane needed.** This is the hard confirmation behind your "universal UniFFI" call:

| | C-lane p99 | UniFFI p99 | |
|---|---|---|---|
| Small (256B–2KB) | 91 ns | 945 ns | sub-µs, negligible |
| Weighted | 347 ns | 2054 ns | |

Surcharged weighted-p99 delta = **2,142 ns = 0.013% of the 16.67ms 60fps budget — 390× below the pre-registered COLLAPSE threshold**, even with a 3× JNI/ARC penalty, robust across 3 runs. The "UniFFI too slow for the push lane" assumption was wrong by ~390×. So **all 4 byte-lane "exception" candidates migrate cleanly — zero internal-ABI exceptions**, including the update-sink hot path.

The review confirms `methodology_sound: true` but `request_changes` on **honesty issues that don't flip the verdict**: the `p99` fields are actually percentiles-of-1000-frame-*means* (smooths the tail — needs relabeling), and the COLLAPSE should carry the explicit "foreign boundary is synthetic/unmeasured" caveat. Assistant: Codex feedback is high-quality — **shape approved** ("the right UniFFI pattern"), with concrete, valid refinements. Key takeaways:

- **Crate:** `crates/nmp-uniffi`, **in-workspace** (the #2149 out-of-workspace was app-specific, not a real constraint); bindgen behind a feature/bin, out of normal `cargo build`.
- **Blocking:** `DispatchOutcome` must carry `{correlation_id, error, code}` — coded rejections are load-bearing in tests, my 2-case enum dropped `code`.
- **High:** don't wrap `nmp-ffi`/parse JSON — **move the FFI-free dispatch core into `nmp-native-runtime`** and wrap that.
- **High:** add explicit idempotent **`shutdown()`** (not just Drop; avoid `close` — Kotlin friction from #2149).
- Preserve start/configure clamps; **drop `pull_page`** from this slice (it's ADR-0058 mirror, → C7); quiescence is preservable via the runtime's existing `set_update_listener` gate.
- **Missed:** the pre-start composition story — scope #2389 as the **base runtime object** + document that storage/projection/capability/signer registration seams layer in via C2/C5/C6.
